name: webhook-delivery-latency
title: Mitigate webhook delivery latency
description: Fix the webhook delivery latency. HEADLINE (Problem 1): a 10-minute window of ZERO inbound requests, coupled to the official client not having the chat OPEN. ROOT CAUSE CONVERGED (2026-11-01): Budva does not own the acquisition boundary of its ruleset sources — it never OpenChat's, so for open-state-gated classes (channels/supergroups) its own session is not an active acquirer and goes silent until some session opens the chat. FIX CONVERGED: OpenChat each channel/supergroup source on Budva's own session and keep it open (the in-process TDlib engine already owns gap-recovery + periodic getChannelDifference re-poll). Producer-side only; receiver is a black box. Secondary (Problem 2): steady-state per-message endpoint HOL (<=60 s at timeoutSeconds:60) — DOWNGRADED to 'potential, unobserved', does not gate Problem 1.
scope: producer side only; receiver is a black box. PROBLEM 1 (HEADLINE, CONVERGED): the 10-min zero-request window is coupled to the official client NOT having the chat open (separate sessions). Root cause = Budva never OpenChat's -> its session is not an active acquirer for open-state-gated classes (channels/supergroups, any size, no protocol threshold); gap-recovery + periodic getChannelDifference re-poll in the pinned TDlib engine are gated on open/member state; a never-opened non-member channel is dropped, not recovered; recovery happens when ANOTHER session opens the chat (cross-session passive updates) = the observed open->burst / close->silence. Fix = OpenChat each channel/supergroup source on Budva's own session + keep open (one OpenChat per source, not one held at a time; open-once-keep, re-open only at re-auth/restart edges); private/basic-group sources are NOT OpenChat'd (not open-state-gated, ride the global stream) -> 'support every type' = one intent (own the acquisition boundary) by each class's own client-conformant mechanism. Three-layer evidence (normative spec core.telegram.org/api/updates + pinned TDlib commit 22d49d5 MessagesManager.cpp + go-tdlib v0.7.6 CGO-over-C++-TDlib architecture); NO owner-run boundary experiment required (withdrawn). PROBLEM 2 (SECONDARY, DOWNGRADED to potential/unobserved): serial per-endpoint worker + cap-256 buffer + single-attempt sink (dispatcher.go:214-237,16,86; delivery.go:133-139,167-172) = <=60 s bounded contributor, G/G/1 (wait linear in service times ahead, not exponential); NO owner-observed per-message delay yet -> verified by a controlled slow-receiver test only if such delay is ever seen; its 4 contract decisions (loss/duplicate/ordering/receiver-T+fast-ack) do NOT gate Problem 1. durable external queue (NATS or equivalent) only under a must-not-lose policy; no bespoke queue microservice. Record reset off main (bb0519b) 2026-11-01; on branch docs/10-30-type-agnostic-requirement pending owner sign-off.
creator: killbus
notes: PHASE = research + design CONVERGED for Problem 1 (pre-implementation). STATUS 2026-11-01: root cause + fix direction converged; record reset off main (bb0519b) and on branch docs/10-30-type-agnostic-requirement pending owner sign-off; NOT committed (owner gate: no commit until root cause + fix are settled — now settled). PROBLEM 1 (HEADLINE) ROOT CAUSE (converged): the 10-min ZERO-request window (text+media) is coupled to the official client NOT having the chat OPEN. Budva is a PASSIVE subscriber that never calls OpenChat/CloseChat/ViewMessages/getChannelDifference (source-verified; the ViewedMessages symbols are its own forwarding-stats counter). For open-state-gated classes (channels/supergroups, any size — no protocol threshold; 'large' is a maintainer paraphrase, NOT a protocol class) the pinned TDlib engine gates gap-recovery + periodic getChannelDifference re-poll on open/member state, so a never-opened session is not an active acquirer and goes silent until ANOTHER session opens the chat (cross-session passive updates for non-member accessible channels) = the observed open->burst / close->silence. THREE-LAYER EVIDENCE (closes it; NO owner-run experiment required, withdrawn): (1) normative spec core.telegram.org/api/updates — passive updates for member channels may stop/reduce; clients (user accounts) should periodically getChannelDifference for currently-viewed (opened) channels; non-final -> re-invoke immediately, final -> after returned timeout (else 1s); 'may also enable passive reception ... to ALL logged-in sessions, as long as ANY session keeps polling'; 'stop polling once closed: may continue only if member'; 'limit to 10 max short-polled'. (2) pinned TDlib commit 22d49d5 (the exact commit go-tdlib v0.7.6 pins) td/telegram/MessagesManager.cpp: open_dialog(:19524) CHECK(!is_bot)+open_count+++was_opened=true (read_history_inbox only in empty-chat edge -> a normal open does NOT mark read); add_pending_channel_update(:7206) on a pts gap: if(was_opened||is_member||sponsored) get_channel_difference ELSE drop; on_update_channel_too_long(:6274) triggers get_channel_difference; on_get_channel_difference reads returned timeout_ and `if(timeout>0 && d->open_count>0) add_timeout_in` -> the periodic poll SELF-CONTINUES only while the dialog stays open; close_dialog(:19640) open_count-- to 0 stops the poll; MAX_CONCURRENT_GET_CHANNEL_DIFFERENCES=10(:36860) engine-caps simultaneous diff polls; retry backs off 1s->x2->cap 60-80s. (3) go-tdlib v0.7.6 is a CGO shell over the C++ TDlib engine (client/tdlib.go: #include <td/telegram/td_json_client.h>, td_execute/td_receive, links -ltdjson) -> the full engine (incl. the channel-difference poller) ALREADY runs inside Budva; the Go side only sends the app-level OpenChat (wrapper present client/function.go:7790). FIX (converged): OpenChat each channel/supergroup source on Budva's own session + KEEP open (no CloseChat except on ruleset removal). Open once, keep — no periodic re-open (poll self-continues while open_count>0; re-open only at state-reset edges: re-auth [dialogs reset] + process restart [open_count in-process]). Keep ALL sources open (one OpenChat per source, not one held at a time; rotation/closing drops that channel's acquirer = re-introduces its silence). Private/basic-group NOT OpenChat'd (global stream, common message-ID sequence + getDifference; not open-state-gated; a client doesn't open every chat). 'Support every type' = one intent (own the acquisition boundary) by each class's own client-conformant mechanism; chat type is DIAGNOSTIC only (selects which mechanism; each is a known fact) — does NOT block the design. Native, no new component, NO hand-built poller. SCALE (engine-enforced, Budva need not write it): engine caps simultaneous diff polls at 10, re-polls at the server-returned timeout (server-paced), no open/close churn; with >10 sources the engine queues them (11th waits) so not all are strictly real-time at very large N — an inherent trade-off, NOT a reason to keep only one open. CONFORMANCE (benchmark = 'what would an official client do'): mechanism layer 0 risk (all standard user RPCs); single-chat shape conformant (open-once-keep = an unclosed tab/dialog, a real client terminal state); combined/scale shape = desktop multi-window client behavior, NOT typical of a phone user (correcting an earlier over-claim 'most client-like N-open'); only distinguishable at large N or if the Budva account is the owner's daily phone account; if a dedicated forwarding account, footprint is self-contained (opening its subscribed channels reads as MORE like a real active user). inherent (document don't mitigate): view/active counts (footprint IS the fix). dissolved: compliance (dedicated-account/DC-IP/flood — user-account daemon is the product's pre-existing architecture; marginal profile = 'a user who keeps N channels open'); read receipts (a client does NOT mark a channel read on openChat — that's a separate readHistory-class call the UI issues; conformance = Budva never calls any read API = the default). GUARDRAILS: (1) open only ruleset source chats, never the account's other chats; (2) stagger the initial/re-auth OpenChat batch (reuse internal/service/limiter), no N openChat in the same instant; (3) open-once-keep, no periodic toggle (churn = the non-human signature + reintroduces the bug); (4) do not fight the engine's 10 cap. CORRECTIONS to earlier record (honest): (1) 'ChannelPoller.cpp' was INVENTED (does not exist; GitHub code search 0 results) — the poller lives in MessagesManager; (2) 'go-tdlib has no GetChannelDifference wrapper -> Budva must hand-build a raw Send poller' was the WRONG direction — go-tdlib is a CGO shell over the C++ TDlib engine which already polls; Budva only sends OpenChat; (3) source-confirm (a) RESOLVED: the pinned TDlib DOES auto-poll an opened channel's difference (open_count>0 re-arm). PROBLEM 1 remaining work: (a) lifecycle + stagger design (re-auth re-open, hot-reload add/remove, limiter-staggered initial batch) against the seams at cmd/engine/main.go:168 / main.go:183-196 — an implementation-design step; (b) OWNER GO-AHEAD to implement. ALL THREE source-confirms are RESOLVED (2026-11-01, by reading the pinned source, no experiment): (1) idle-open delivery = UNCONDITIONAL re-poll — the re-arm `if (timeout>0 && d->open_count>0) add_timeout_in` is on the SUCCESS path of on_get_channel_difference (MessagesManager.cpp:37423) with NO gap check, and the timer handler on_channel_get_difference_timeout (:36707) fires get_channel_difference unconditionally → an idle-but-open channel stays near-real-time → FIX FORM = literally 'one OpenChat + keep open', NO re-poll nudge; (2) >10 behavior = UNBOUNDED FIFO pending queue, NO loss, NO starvation — do_get_channel_difference pushes to pending_get_channel_differences_ (:36854), drained only while count<10 (:36860-36863), each completion re-drains, one outstanding request per chat; with >10 open sources: 10 in flight, the rest rotate at their own server timeout, a large-backlog channel re-queues its next page immediately (per-page FIFO fairness); the 11th+ is DEFERRED NEVER DROPPED; (3) member-channel idle delivery = DECISION keep the open set = ALL channel/supergroup sources, do NOT shrink to non-member only — the spec sends passive member updates 'usually' but 'in some cases may stop (or send fewer)' (NOT a guarantee), and the engine gap-recovery gate (:7206) treats was_opened and is_member as separate sufficiency conditions; the saved volume is small vs the risk of re-introducing the silence; a member reduction is a later optimization requiring production evidence, not preset. Then implement (native, small): the OpenChat set for channel/supergroup sources at generation build + re-auth + hot-reload edges with the stagger guardrail; a regression test asserting the open set matches the ruleset's channel/supergroup sources (NOTE: this test asserts OpenChat is CALLED correctly; it cannot assert updates arrive in real time — that needs a live TDlib + server, so the final acceptance is post-deploy observation on the box). ENTRY GATE (Problem 1 code change blocked until closed): root cause + fix recorded & converged (done); source-confirms 1-3 RESOLVED against the pinned source (2026-11-01); lifecycle + stagger guardrails designed against the seams; OWNER GO-AHEAD to implement (a decision, NOT an input). NO owner-run experiment, NO Problem-2 contract, NO source-chat-type answer required to proceed. PROBLEM 2 (SECONDARY, DOWNGRADED to potential/unobserved): serial per-endpoint worker (dispatcher.go:214-237) + cap-256 buffer (dispatcher.go:16,86) + single-attempt sink (delivery.go:133-139, worker occupied until response delivery.go:167-172) = a real code property but NO owner-observed per-message queueing delay -> per the 'does the problem even hold' criterion it is a POTENTIAL contributor, not yet a problem; separate leg from Problem 1; does NOT gate the Problem-1 fix. G/G/1: stability rho=lambda*E[B]<1 (timeout only an upper bound on B, 1/timeout a worst-case LOWER service-rate bound); wait(k)<=requests_ahead*timeout (worst-case upper bound, LINEAR not exponential). Evidence gate IF pursued = a controlled slow-receiver test (in-repo, fixed T, reproduces queue-wait growth linearly, race-clean, CI-runnable), NOT production timing collection. Its 4 contract decisions (loss/duplicate/ordering/receiver-T+fast-ack) are THIS leg's blockers only. EXCLUDED: bespoke in-repo queue microservice; in-budva durable outbox+retry (thickens budva); B' local-outbox+reader; a HAND-BUILT Go getChannelDifference poller for Problem 1 (rejected because the C++ engine already polls — go-tdlib is a CGO shell); preset concurrency/timeout; production timing collection as a gate; full T1-T4 tracing platform; durable external queue (NATS JetStream or Redis Stream, NOT pre-approved by name) + queueSink via the existing push.Sink seam (dispatcher.go:32-36) only under a must-not-lose policy. Baseline code main@415d90c (10-29 fix); record reset to bb0519b. Related: [[trellis-task-10-29-budva-push-stall]], [[github-push-dispatch-mechanics]], [[merge-requires-explicit-user-approval]].
